analysis.title: Buying Into The Muse-Hype - Thoughts Into 3Q Earnings
key_insights: DB's 3Q channel checks suggest core advertising at Meta remains strong, helped by higher engagement and ROAS-driven CPM growth.
DB raises its 3Q consolidated revenue estimate to $63.7bn from $63.1bn, implying +25.4% y/y FXN growth. The buyside is thought to be modestly above the $64bn high end of the 3Q revenue guide.
Buyside expectations for the high end of 4Q26 consolidated revenue outlook are roughly $74-74.5bn.
The Muse consumer agent shows relatively durable downloads and adoption, which DB reads as significant early US consumer demand for personal AI agents.

DB expects direct monetization of Muse to come as the platform scales, consistent with Meta's scale-then-monetize pattern. Routes named are subscriptions, a commerce take-rate model, interchange spread, and advertising on Muse's Feed tab.
DB suspects the stock keeps trading on Muse downloads, users, engagement and retention near term, plus new model launches that have put Meta back in the frontier discussion.
Costs are a clear debate. DB argues much of the capacity expansion and current CapEx is directed at scaling products like Muse and so should not be incremental.
Investors expect FY27 Opex of $210-225bn and CapEx of $230-240bn, and expect directional FY27 guidance this quarter as Meta gave in 3Q25.
DB raises its FY27 Opex estimate to $210bn from $204bn and CapEx to $232bn from $214bn. Greater use of Meta's own Muse models could moderate token expenses.

Meta could use Muse to offer a 'business in a box' solution to the >200mn SMBs on its platforms. Channel checks show savings from agentic customer service being shifted to demand generation, which translates into ad revenue.
Recent model launches (Muse Wonder Family) mean Meta increasingly screens as a frontier lab, which could open subscription and enterprise revenue as companies seek efficiency in AI spend.
DB reiterates Buy and a $820 price target, based on 27x 2027E earnings, up from 25x, to reflect strong Muse adoption.

One agency said Meta's two-year growth stack finished about 200bps ahead of initial expectations and raised 4Q and 1Q forecasts. A second check showed y/y spend growth accelerating about 200bps through 3Q. A third showed acceleration from 2Q26 to 3Q, citing ROI gains from 1Q26 AI-based creative and audience tools.
The checks compare with Street expectations of about 150bps of FX-neutral deceleration, supporting potential upside to advertising estimates.
CPM growth accelerated about 350bps sequentially in 3Q after about 650bps in 2Q, supported by better click-through and conversion, a richer Reels and Stories mix and Audience Network gains.
Business Agents are driving incremental spend among smaller advertisers. One expert's micro-advertiser cohort grew about four times faster than its largest-advertiser cohort.
DB projects 3Q advertising revenue growth of +24.8% y/y FXN, about 1pt slower than 2Q26, against a roughly 3pt tougher comp.
Likely call questions: Muse monetization timeline, enterprise ambitions, owned-and-operated vs third-party capacity split in FY27, longer-term capital intensity and funding sources.

Sensor Tower data show Muse downloads and daily active users well ahead of other AI apps post-launch, including Sora, but significantly behind ChatGPT. Time spent on Muse is well ahead of similar apps, above current Gemini time spent and approaching ChatGPT.

market_movers.rationale: Reiterates Buy and $820 target on 27x 2027E earnings, raised from 25x on Muse adoption. Channel checks point to upside to 3Q advertising estimates.

sector_views.rationale: Agentic tools are shifting small-business costs toward demand generation, which benefits advertising platforms such as Meta.

earnings_insights: Meta 3Q26: DB consolidated revenue estimate $63.7bn (raised from $63.1bn), +25.4% y/y FXN, against company guide high end of $64bn. Estimate, not reported.
Meta 3Q26: DB advertising revenue estimate +24.8% y/y FXN, about 1pt decel from 2Q26 on a roughly 3pt tougher comp. Estimate, not reported.
Meta 4Q26: buyside expects the high end of the revenue outlook at roughly $74-74.5bn consolidated revenue (investor expectation, not guidance).
Meta FY27: DB estimates Opex $210bn (from $204bn) and CapEx $232bn (from $214bn). Investor expectations are Opex $210-225bn and CapEx $230-240bn. Estimates, not company guidance.
risk_factors: Rising Opex and CapEx for AI and Muse scaling, with the funding sources a likely investor question.
Muse monetization is likely delayed under a scale-then-monetize approach, leaving the stock sensitive to download, user and retention trends.
Muse remains significantly behind ChatGPT in downloads and DAUs, and a powerful agent could see lower usage time than a chatbot at stabilization.
Advertising growth faces a roughly 3pt tougher comparison in 3Q.
charts_described: Figure 1 shows Muse usage and download data for the US from Sensor Tower, with downloads and DAUs well ahead of other AI apps post-launch but behind ChatGPT, per the accompanying text.
vol_and_positioning: Buyside is described as modestly above the 3Q revenue guide of $64bn, and the stock is expected to trade near term on Muse downloads, users, engagement and retention.

tension_points.bull_case: Much of capacity expansion and current CapEx is directed at scaling products like Muse, so it should not be incremental. Muse adoption is strong, and DB sees the start of a rich product cycle that foreshadows returns on AI investment.
tension_points.bear_case: Costs are the subject of a clear debate. DB's FY27 Opex and CapEx estimates rise to $210bn and $232bn, and investors expect FY27 CapEx of $230-240bn with funding sources an open question.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Muse download, user, engagement and retention trends weakening, or FY27 Opex and CapEx guidance well above investor expectations of $210-225bn and $230-240bn.
